items.label: ROAST
items.title: Roast Levels
items.summary: Light to dark: how the roast shifts taste before you even brew.
items.fact: There is no “best” roast. It is a flavour choice, not a quality scale.

items.label: GRIND SIZE
items.title: Grind Size
items.summary: Coarse to fine: the dial that controls how fast flavour extracts.
items.fact: Grind is usually the first thing to change when a cup tastes off.

items.label: EXTRACTION
items.title: The Extraction Spectrum
items.summary: Under to over: the one idea behind sour vs bitter.
items.fact: Water dissolves the sour notes first and the bitter ones last. Time decides where you stop.

items.label: RATIO
items.title: Coffee-to-Water Ratio
items.summary: How much coffee vs water sets the strength of your cup.
items.fact: Most brews land near 1:16, one gram of coffee to sixteen of water.

items.label: CHERRY ANATOMY
items.title: Cherry Anatomy
items.summary: Six layers between the skin of the fruit and the seed you brew.
items.fact: Layer 03, the sticky mucilage, is the one washed, honey and natural argue over.

items.label: VARIETY
items.title: The Variety Family Tree
items.summary: Typica and Bourbon: the two old parents behind most cups you’ll meet.
items.fact: Geisha, Caturra and SL28 are all arabica. Variety is why they taste nothing alike.

items.label: CAFFEINE
items.title: Caffeine, Per Serving
items.summary: What each brew actually delivers. The serving matters as much as the method.
items.fact: A single espresso carries less caffeine than a mug of drip.

items.label: GRIND SPREAD
items.title: Particle Distribution
items.summary: Why a burr’s tight spread beats a blade’s fines-and-boulders.
items.fact: Even a cheap burr grinder beats a blade: evenness matters more than fineness.
